diagnoses.description: Date disambiguation failure: the pipeline selected a secondary date-like token (likely from a different header line or OCR-corrupted label) instead of the primary header “Date:” field in the invoice header block.
diagnoses.evidence: Allowed feedback: 034.jpg date_correct=false while amount_correct=true; prediction date=2018-08-09. Visual inspection of 034.jpg shows a clear header block with “Date: 09/03/2018” near the top, while other date-like strings can appear elsewhere (and prior history shows DATE→DATA corruption). This is a classic multi-candidate selection problem requiring label-tolerant matching plus explicit preference for the primary header Date field (top-of-receipt).

locations.section: Field Extraction Heuristics (Receipts) / Date extraction (reduce false positives)

diagnoses.description: Total selection failure due to OCR digit-flip outlier and competing total-like lines: the chosen total (702.00) contradicts multiple internal anchors on the same receipt (Subtotal/Total incl/Total Amt Rounded/Payment) that agree on 102.00.
diagnoses.evidence: Allowed feedback: 074.jpg amount_correct=false while date_correct=true; prediction total_amount=702.00. Visual inspection of 074.jpg shows Subtotal 102.00, Total incl. of GST 102.00, Total Amt Rounded 102.00, Payment 102.00; 702.00 is a typical OCR 1→7 digit flip. The historical run also shows that OCR configuration changes (grayscale+autocontrast + PSM6 and/or upscaling) can remove the corrupted 702.00 line, so selection must apply an anchor-consistency override rather than trusting a single keyword line or “last TOTAL wins”.

diagnoses.description: Rounding precedence failure: the extractor selected the pre-rounding inclusive total (23.26) instead of the final payable TOTAL after a rounding adjustment (23.25).
diagnoses.evidence: Allowed feedback: 077.jpg amount_correct=false while date_correct=true; prediction total_amount=23.26. Visual inspection of 077.jpg shows “Total (Inclusive of GST): 23.26”, then “Rounding Adj: -0.01”, then a bold final “TOTAL: 23.25”. Exact-match scoring requires a mechanical precedence rule: if a rounding adjustment exists and a later TOTAL exists, always take the later TOTAL.

locations.section: Field Extraction Heuristics (Receipts) / Rounding handling (common exact-match failure) — HARD RULE

diagnoses.description: Coupled extraction + schema failure: total_amount was emitted as an empty string instead of null; additionally, this receipt layout contains an “Amount” column header that can trigger split-line fallback to an item amount unless explicitly excluded, and OCR may corrupt both the GRAND TOTAL keyword and decimal separator (e.g., 92:80).
diagnoses.evidence: Allowed feedback: 078.jpg amount_correct=false; prediction total_amount="" violates task requirement (must be null on failure). Visual inspection of 078.jpg shows a table header “Description Qty Price Amount” and summary lines “Total: 92.80” / “Grand Total: 92.80” plus payment lines “Cash Received: 100.00”, “Change: 7.20”. Prior history shows header-triggered split-line fallback and punctuation corruption (92:80) and keyword corruption (GrandTota./GrandTotal.), which require explicit header exclusion, tight fallback gating, decimal normalization, and a final schema guard (empty/whitespace → null).

quality_impact.rationale: The current candidate image-ocr skill already encodes the minimal, transferable fixes implied by the historical failures: header/label-tolerant date ranking (034), anchor-driven outlier rejection and conditional upscale OCR passes (074), hard rounding precedence (077), explicit exclusion of AMOUNT column headers + tight split-line fallback + tolerant GRAND TOTAL matching + decimal-separator normalization + empty-string→null guard (078). Additional edits would be largely redundant; remaining risk is downstream implementation adherence rather than missing skill guidance.

trigger_precision.rationale: Existing guidance is narrowly scoped to receipt OCR and triggers only under specific conditions (e.g., split-line fallback only when keyword line has no digits and is not a header; anchor override only when multiple anchors agree; optional upscaling only as fallback). No additional broadening is needed.

instruction_compliance.rationale: Diagnoses rely only on permitted evidence (field-level correctness feedback, predictions, and provided images/OCR snippets). No oracle values are referenced. No tool execution is requested. No unnecessary skill files are modified.

solution_path_coverage.rationale: Covers all observed failure classes in the run: wrong date among multiple candidates (034), wrong total due to OCR digit flip/outlier (074), wrong total due to rounding precedence (077), and schema/normalization + header-triggered fallback issues (078).

skillaxe_evaluation.overall_rationale: The packet’s evidence indicates the original run’s misses were dominated by receipt-specific selection/normalization under OCR noise, not missing OCR capability. The current candidate image-ocr skill already contains the necessary heuristics; the most effective next step is ensuring implementations actually apply them (anchor-consistency override, rounding precedence, header-line exclusion, and final schema guard).

iteration_summary: Diagnosed the four incorrect fields (034 date; 074/077/078 totals) using allowed feedback and the provided images. No SKILL.md updates proposed because the current candidate image-ocr skill already addresses these failure modes; remaining risk is implementation adherence rather than missing guidance.
